# @uptimizr/metrics

> The semantic metric registry for Uptimizr: one machine-readable definition per analytics metric —
> endpoint, filters, Zod row schema, per-column units, row limits, interpretation and caveats,
> plus the Zod mirrors of the `format=full | table | summary` result envelopes.
> Pure data, browser-safe: the only runtime dependencies are `zod` and `@uptimizr/schema`.

## Docs

- [Package reference](./README.md): install, the `MetricDefinition` fields, every export, how to add a metric.
- [Agent guide](./AGENTS.md): rules and canonical usage for AI agents.
- [Query API reference](https://uptimizr.com/docs/api/query/): the endpoints these metrics describe.
- [Architecture Decision Records](https://github.com/RaananW/Uptimizr/tree/main/docs/adr): ADR 0051 (AI-first analytics layer), ADR 0050 (browser-safe agent core).

## Key exports

- `METRIC_REGISTRY` / `METRIC_IDS` — every metric, keyed by its stable snake_case id (which is also the MCP tool name).
- `allMetrics()`, `getMetric(id)`, `isMetricId(value)`, `metricForBuilder(name)`, and the three entry-kind predicates `isResourceMetric` (a store read: no builder, no querystring, no `format`), `isDerivedMetric` (computed in TypeScript over other metrics — the five insight primitives `insight_baseline`, `insight_movers`, `insight_anomalies`, `insight_significance` and `insight_scene_health`, ADR 0051 §4; `insight_significance` picks its test from the compared metric's own `columns[...].rateOf`, and `insight_scene_health` publishes its per-factor weights in its `caveats`) and `isAggregateMetric` (either, i.e. "takes a querystring"). Prefer `isAggregateMetric` over `metric.builder != null`, or a derived metric silently drops out of the envelope and OpenAPI surfaces.
- `FILTER_TARGETS` — every request parameter and what it does; `DIMENSION_COLUMNS` — every group-by dimension.
- `AGGREGATION_BUILDER_NAMES` — the closed set of `build*` aggregations in `@uptimizr/db`.
- `resultFormatSchema`, `tableEnvelopeSchema(row)`, `summaryEnvelopeSchema`, `tableMetaSchema` — the `format` envelopes as Zod (ADR 0051 §2).
- `resultEnvelopeSchema(row, full?)` — the union of the three; `structuredEnvelopeSchema(row)` — the merged object form an MCP `outputSchema` needs.
- The grain is registry data: `MetricDefinition.grainDimensions` (read it through `nativeDimensions`) is what a row is keyed by, while `dimensions` is everything the metric can be filtered, keyed or regrouped by. A metric that also declares `genericGroupBy` can be recomputed at any grain in `genericDimensions(metric)` by the shared group-by builder in `@uptimizr/db`; `queryTier(metric, query)` says which compiler a query takes.
- Types: `MetricDefinition`, `MetricId`, `MetricEndpoint`, `MetricDerivation`, `ColumnSemantics`, `ColumnUnit`, `DimensionId`, `FilterId`, `MetricCategory`, `MetricGrain`, `GenericGroupBy`, `GenericMeasure`, `QueryTier`.

## Rules

- Derive tool catalogs, OpenAPI documents and docs tables from the registry; never restate them by hand.
- A new aggregation is not done until it has a registry entry.
- Keep this package free of `@uptimizr/db`, `node:` built-ins and native dependencies.
- `sourceChannels` is load-bearing beyond documentation: the collector's project context document
  (`GET /api/v1/context`, ADR 0051 §5) reports a metric as `disabledByCapture` when **every** channel
  it declares produced no events over the window. A metric with an empty `sourceChannels` is a
  derived rollup and is never reported as disabled — so declare the channels a metric really reads.
